_comment: Declared run-body failure swallows, enforced by scripts/check-workflow-run-swallow.py
(sparq-org/sparq#5799). An entry here means: this step deliberately discards the
failure of a gate-classified command, and something else in the same job re-raises it.
R2 deletes the entry for you by REDDING once the underlying swallow is gone, so a
stale waiver can never silently pre-approve the next one added to the same step.
Required fields: workflow, job_id, step_name, command, why, registered.
`command` is matched as a SUBSTRING of the offending shell line, so a waiver covers
one command and not the whole step.

run_swallow_waivers.why: Two-step by design: this step captures cargo-deny's status into steps.deny.outputs.exit_code (hence the trailing `exit 0`) so the report can be published to the tracking issue, and the LAST step of the same job — 'Fail the job if advisories were found', gated on `steps.deny.outputs.exit_code != '0'` — re-raises it. Deleting that step is a job-level change, not an invisible shell one.

Miri's raw exit code cannot distinguish UB (fatal) from a shard timeout (known, tracked debt), so the run is captured to a libtest-json stream and the verdict is decided by the next step, 'Classify shard verdict', which runs scripts/miri_classify_verdict.py and fails the job on a UB event.
